cards.why: Joel's rejection rests on his motor-vehicle record (R-101, delivered 7 October), he signed the authorization on 29 September, and no pre-adverse notice has gone. The policy gives 2 business days from the report's arrival, so it is due today, Friday 9 October. FCRA 604(b)(3)(A): the report copy and the summary of rights go together, before the rejection

Paulina's rejection rests on the employment check (R-102, delivered 8 October); her authorization is signed and nothing has been sent. Two business days from 8 October is Tuesday 13 October, because Monday 12 October is a company holiday; it may go today

Desmond's rejection rests in part on the report (the interview scored 2 of 5, and the employment check R-103 shows a dismissal he left off): a decision based in whole or in part on a report needs the notice (604(b)(3)(A)). The report arrived 5 October, so the notice was due 7 October and is overdue; nothing has been sent

Ingrid's notice of 24 September (N-1) carried the copy of the report and no summary of rights, so it did not meet 604(b)(3)(A) and the policy says to send it again complete, with the wait starting from the new date. Only the notice log shows what was attached

Wyatt's complete pre-adverse notice went on Monday 28 September (N-6). Five full business days are 29 September to 5 October, so the sixth business day, 6 October, has passed; no dispute, the report still shows the suspension. 615(a): the notice names Veritarn with address and phone, says it did not decide, and gives the 60-day free copy and the right to dispute

Noreen's complete pre-adverse notice went on Wednesday 30 September (N-7); five full business days run to 7 October, the sixth is 8 October, and her 6 October message says the report is accurate and she has no dispute

Kenji's complete pre-adverse notice went on Thursday 1 October (N-8). The five full business days are 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 October, so today, Friday 9 October, is the sixth business day and the earliest the final notice may go; no dispute

Tomas Brandl wrote on 2 October that the theft record belongs to another man of his name born in 1988; only his message in Postwren shows it, and Veritarn's page logs no dispute. The policy sends the candidate's statement to the vendor the day HR reads it, and holds his final notice

closing_words:
Eight cards are going to you for approval: 4 pre-adverse notices, 3 final notices and 1 dispute forward. Nothing has been sent yet. I'm counting business days from today, Friday 9 Oct, with Monday 12 Oct as a company holiday.

**Pre-adverse notices.** Each one attaches the report copy and the CFPB *Summary of Your Rights*.
- **C-101 Varnham** (R-101, delivered 7 Oct): no notice is in the log.
- **C-102 Sorrel** (R-102, delivered 8 Oct): no notice is in the log.
- **C-103 Hale** (R-103, delivered 5 Oct): no notice is in the log. The 2-business-day window ended 7 Oct, so this one is late. It is still owed, because the rejection rests partly on the report.
- **C-214 Lowe** (R-214): her 24 Sep notice (N-1) went without the summary of rights. It is sent again complete, and the wait restarts from today.


**Final notices.** Each wait has ended and there is no open dispute. Each uses the agency
